name: security-master
purpose: One row per asset with its kind (fiat, stablecoin or crypto); one row per instrument and version of its venue listing (tick size, decimals, minimum order, status, listed or not); and one row per venue spelling and version, the symbol a venue's trades stream carries, with the instrument it names. A version is valid from the first fetch that saw it; the first version of a key opens at 1970-01-01 so that a trade older than the first fetch still resolves; the open version ends at 9999-12-31 23:59:59, never null.
limitations: Kraken only, from its AssetPairs listing, so history starts at that product's first fetch and a version starts up to an hour late. A venue spelling is the listing's websocket name with each code upper-cased and mapped through seeds/code_exceptions.csv, recomposed as base/quote: if the trades stream spells a pair otherwise, its trades resolve to nothing and are held by the trades product. A spelling two pairs of one venue claim at overlapping times is held in venue_symbol_held, and neither claim is published until the owner resolves it. The kind of an asset is fiat when the currency master lists it as a circulating currency with minor units, stablecoin when seeds/stablecoins.csv lists it, else crypto.
usage: Resolve a trade by venue and venue_symbol in reference_data.security_master.venue_symbol with valid_from <= trade time < valid_to, half-open, then read the instrument by venue and instrument_id over the same interval rule. Filter valid_to = TIMESTAMP '9999-12-31 23:59:59 UTC' for the current rows: a query that forgets it reads history.

outputs.purpose: One row per canonical asset code that a published instrument buys or is priced in, with its kind and when a listing first showed it. No history: an asset's code and kind do not change.

columns.name: asset_code
columns.description: The canonical code, upper case, a venue's older code already mapped (BTC, USD).

columns.name: kind
columns.description: fiat when the currency master lists the code as a circulating currency (not a fund, with minor units, so not a metal, the SDR or a testing code); stablecoin when seeds/stablecoins.csv lists it; else crypto.

columns.name: first_seen_at
columns.description: The first fetch whose listing showed an instrument with this asset, in UTC.

quality.name: kind_is_known
quality.description: Every asset is fiat, stablecoin or crypto.

outputs.purpose: Type-2: one row per instrument of a venue and version of its listing, valid from valid_from up to but not including valid_to. A version is a change in the pair that lists it, its tick size, decimals, minimum order or status, or whether it is listed at all: a delisting closes the listed version and opens one with is_listed false, a relisting opens another.

columns.name: venue
columns.description: The venue that lists the instrument (kraken).

columns.name: instrument_id
columns.description: <base_asset>-<quote_asset> of canonical codes (BTC-USD); the same on every venue.

columns.name: valid_from
columns.description: The fetch that first saw this version, in UTC; the instrument's first version opens at 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.

columns.name: valid_to
columns.description: The next version's valid_from; 9999-12-31 23:59:59 UTC on the open row, never null.

columns.name: recorded_at
columns.description: When the fetch that first saw this version ran, in UTC (knowledge time).

columns.name: base_asset
columns.description: The canonical code of the asset bought (asset.asset_code).

columns.name: quote_asset
columns.description: The canonical code of the asset it is priced in, an asset.asset_code.

columns.name: is_listed
columns.description: False while no pair of the venue lists the instrument; every listing attribute below is then null.

columns.name: pair_code
columns.description: The venue's REST code of the pair that lists it.

columns.name: tick_size
columns.description: The smallest price step.

columns.name: pair_decimals
columns.description: Digits after the decimal point of a price.

columns.name: lot_decimals
columns.description: Digits after the decimal point of a volume.

columns.name: order_min
columns.description: The smallest order volume in the base asset.

columns.name: status
columns.description: The pair's trading status as the venue states it (online, cancel_only and the like).

quality.name: versions_do_not_overlap
quality.description: Each version ends no later than the next one of its key starts.

quality.name: versions_leave_no_gap
quality.description: Each version ends exactly where the next one of its key starts.

quality.name: one_open_row_per_key
quality.description: Every instrument of a venue has exactly one open row.

quality.name: first_version_opens_1970
quality.description: Every instrument's first version opens at 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.

quality.name: intervals_not_empty
quality.description: Every version is valid for some time.

outputs.purpose: Type-2: one row per venue spelling and version, the symbol the venue's trades stream carries and the instrument it names, valid from valid_from up to but not including valid_to. A trade resolves through the row of its venue and symbol whose interval holds its time. A version changes when the instrument or the pair behind the spelling changes; a delisting does not close it (the instrument's is_listed records that), so the spelling still resolves.

columns.name: venue
columns.description: The venue (kraken).

columns.name: venue_symbol
columns.description: The symbol as the venue's trades stream spells it (BTC/USD on Kraken's websocket v2).

columns.name: valid_from
columns.description: The fetch that first saw this version, in UTC; the spelling's first version opens at 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.

columns.name: valid_to
columns.description: The next version's valid_from; 9999-12-31 23:59:59 UTC on the open row, never null.

columns.name: instrument_id
columns.description: The instrument the spelling names (instrument.instrument_id).

columns.name: pair_code
columns.description: The venue's REST code of the pair whose listing claims the spelling.

columns.name: recorded_at
columns.description: When the fetch that first saw this version ran, in UTC (knowledge time).

quality.name: versions_do_not_overlap
quality.description: Each version ends no later than the next one of its key starts.

quality.name: versions_leave_no_gap
quality.description: Each version ends exactly where the next one of its key starts.

quality.name: one_open_row_per_key
quality.description: Every spelling of a venue has exactly one open row.

quality.name: first_version_opens_1970
quality.description: Every spelling's first version opens at 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.

quality.name: intervals_not_empty
quality.description: Every version is valid for some time.

outputs.purpose: One row per span in which a venue's pair is listed with one set of attributes: the listing's websocket name resolved by rule into canonical base and quote codes, the venue spelling and instrument id composed from them, and whether the claim is held. The one place the matching rule lives: instrument and venue_symbol publish the claims that are not held, and venue_symbol_held lists the ones that are.

columns.name: venue
columns.description: The venue whose listing states the pair (kraken).

columns.name: pair_code
columns.description: The pair's REST code in the venue's listing.

columns.name: claimed_from
columns.description: The first fetch that stated this listing of the pair (the listing version's first_fetched_at), in UTC.

columns.name: claimed_to
columns.description: The pair's next listing version, changed or unlisted; 9999-12-31 23:59:59 UTC while none follows.

columns.name: ws_name
columns.description: The websocket name as the listing spells it.

columns.name: base_asset
columns.description: The canonical base code: the websocket name's part before its one slash, upper-cased, then mapped through seeds/code_exceptions.csv for the venue. Null when the name is not of the form base/quote.

columns.name: quote_asset
columns.description: The canonical quote code, by the same rule from the part after the slash; null as base_asset is.

columns.name: venue_symbol
columns.description: base_asset/quote_asset, the spelling the venue's trades stream carries; null when either is.

columns.name: instrument_id
columns.description: base_asset-quote_asset, the canonical instrument id; null when either is.

columns.name: tick_size
columns.description: The smallest price step the listing states.

columns.name: pair_decimals
columns.description: Digits after the decimal point of a price.

columns.name: lot_decimals
columns.description: Digits after the decimal point of a volume.

columns.name: order_min
columns.description: The smallest order volume in the base asset.

columns.name: status
columns.description: The pair's trading status as the venue states it.

columns.name: held_reason
columns.description: Null for a claim that is published. claimed_twice: another pair of the venue claims the same venue_symbol over an overlapping span, so every claim of that spelling is held. not_base_slash_quote: the websocket name has no single slash to split.

outputs.purpose: The claims held from publication: every claim of a spelling two pairs of one venue claim at overlapping times, and every listing whose websocket name the rule cannot split. Other spellings and other venues publish as usual. Owner-only.

columns.name: venue
columns.description: The venue whose listing states the pair.

columns.name: pair_code
columns.description: The pair's REST code.

columns.name: claimed_from
columns.description: The first fetch that stated this listing of the pair, in UTC.

columns.name: claimed_to
columns.description: The pair's next listing version; 9999-12-31 23:59:59 UTC while none follows.

columns.name: ws_name
columns.description: The websocket name as the listing spells it.

columns.name: venue_symbol
columns.description: The spelling the rule composed; null when the name could not be split.

columns.name: held_reason
columns.description: claimed_twice or not_base_slash_quote (venue_symbol_claim.held_reason).

quality.name: no_claim_held
quality.description: No claim is held; a held one warns and the build still publishes the rest.
